summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.2/14)

data.turoyo: Kətwulle ḥasyo du čaġawo, lə kuḏaʕno əšme, saləq bi mədde du ḥarabano kule fayəš ʕal i goro, duʕewo, buxewo, ṣuyamwo w mṣalewo qm Aloho, Aloho d oṯe bi raḥme ʕal u šaʕb da mšiḥoye, d xulṣi w u mede d fayəš d lə məqṭoli.
data.translation: Sie hatten damals einen Bischof, dessen Namen ich nicht weiß, der stieg auf das Dach und blieb dort den ganzen Krieg über, er flehte, weinte, fastete und betete zu Gott, Gott möge Erbarmen mit dem Volk der Christen haben, damit sie entkämen und die, die noch übrig waren, nicht auch noch getötet würden.

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1; prayer qm Aloho in a sustained wartime sequence.

summary: All securely identified Turoyo tokens continue II.1 beten, Gottesdienst abhalten; no new numbered sense. German segnen in the bread and clothes rituals describes the effect of prayer, while the Turoyo ʕal construction is already represented at 40/30.

Valency: unexpressed prayer content is common; ṣluṯo can be a zero-marked cognate object (JL 5.10/2, /9; 66/60; 94/33) or resumed by -la (68/45). Divine addressee m Aloho (24/2), qm Aloho (JTM 3.2/14), beneficiaries l- or lašan-, and language b səryoyo are distinct from L-marked Preterit agents (JTM 1.3/12).

Infectum covers ongoing, habitual, purposive and prospective prayer; Infectum-wa presents recurrent past practice; Part act. occurs in durable devotion and plural coordinated predicates. Detransitive kmiṣale at 11/75 suppresses the human officiant with church location bənne.

The Imperativ has ṣalawu in PrS and Mṣalawu in JTM; do not silently regularize either. Feminine first-person dəmṣalyono in MAC NE interview 1/8 is an Infectum purpose clause, distinct from the Part act. mṣalyono at 11/75.

Duplicate citations were not re-added (JL 19.6/17; 40/30; PrS 56/5). Reader questions claiming a missing translation at MAC NE interview 1/23 are obsolete for this supplied input, which contains the clauses.
No independently lexicalized idiom is established: praying a prayer and praying over ritual targets remain under sense 1.
Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals remain prior material and are not re-proposed here.

The supplied Jan material includes conversational interviews as well as prose. Ordinary forms corroborate II.1 rather than adding a literary sense. Habitual -wa dominates retrospective ministry; k- Infectum can also background prayer at a killing (Jan 2.2/62).
Jan 3.17/304 contrasts mṣalele with mṣalewayle and an overt l ḥasyo agent. Other mṣalewole tokens are less secure because an Infectum-wa recipient suffix is also possible.
Jan Detransitive miṣale suppresses the officiant but retains prayer content, ʕal targets or -lən recipients; lazəm takes d miṣale in the language-of-worship report.
Jan 3.46/1259 supplies a resumed cognate object in Imperativ, supporting round-1 object coding. The Imperativ box was already proposed in round 1.
mṣalalle recurs in otherwise ordinary prayer contexts; mšalelilən at Jan 2.10/2180 is isolated beside Mṣaleli. Quoted Syriac mṣalenan and Naṣal are excluded from the Turoyo paradigm.

Resolve 69/275: Adlalyo kəmṣaleno lacks the negation and “here” present in the German. Confirm gəmṣaləṭ spelling at 69/272 and the plural -ən alongside ṣaymi at PrS 56/13.
The inherited 40/30 English has “a prayed”; check the editorial source before correcting its wording. Quoted Syriac nṣale (94/41) is excluded from the Turoyo paradigm.

Confirm mṣalewole segmentation at Jan 1.38/1587, 2.4/1059 and 2.6/1689 against clear mṣalewayle l ḥasyo at 3.17/304.
Is mšalelilən at Jan 2.10/2180 a transcription error? Confirm mṣalalle variants and the community suffix in Mṣalewaynanne (3.31/861).

summary: ʕal marks prayer targets including bread, clothes, a bridal couple, a deceased person and a chick. These ritual participant extensions do not require a separate blessing sense.

Jan supports round-1 ritual target extension, including oil and a basin of water with ʕal, graves, and beneficiaries l-/lašan-. A marriage-service book as zero-marked content extends the prayer-text object, without a new sense.
Service for a community shows -lən, free šanayye and uncertain -nanne; retain these surface contrasts without treating -nanne as established direct-object coding.
